# PackageUpdates

`c.PackageUpdates` calls the API's PackageUpdates group. The updates the package
index has for the host.

## Methods

| Method                             | Returns                                          | Permission      | Description                                        |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| [`List(ctx, hostname)`](#list)     | `*Response[Collection[PackageUpdatesAvailable]]` | `package:read`  | List the packages the index has newer versions of. |
| [`Update(ctx, hostname)`](#update) | `*Response[Collection[PackageUpdatesResult]]`    | `package:write` | Refresh the package index.                         |

### List

```go
func (s *PackageUpdatesService) List(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[PackageUpdatesAvailable]], error)
```

List the packages the index has newer versions of.

Runs apt list --upgradable: each package with its installed version and the
version the index has. Refresh the index first for what the repositories have
now.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/package/updates`, and needs the permission
`package:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Two updates, `go run package_updates.go list`:

```go
resp, err := c.PackageUpdates.List(ctx, target)
```

### Update

```go
func (s *PackageUpdatesService) Update(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
) (*Response[Collection[PackageUpdatesResult]], error)
```

Refresh the package index.

Runs apt-get update. It reports changed: true when the Release file of a
repository under /var/lib/apt/lists changed, and changed: false when each
repository was unchanged.

It sends `PUT /api/node/{hostname}/package/updates`, and needs the permission
`package:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

The repositories are unchanged since the last refresh,
`go run package_updates.go update`:

```go
resp, err := c.PackageUpdates.Update(ctx, target)
```
